extraction.name: SQuAD: 100,000+ Questions for Machine Comprehension of Text
extraction.description: The Stanford Question Answering Dataset (SQuAD), a reading comprehension dataset consisting of 100,000+ questions posed by crowdworkers on a set of Wikipedia articles, where the answer to each question is a segment of text from the corresponding reading passage.
extraction.creator: Pranav Rajpurkar, Jian Zhang, Konstantin Lopyrev, Percy Liang
extraction.citeAs: Rajpurkar, P., Zhang, J., Lopyrev, K., & Liang, P. (2016). SQuAD: 100,000+ Questions for Machine Comprehension of Text.
extraction.rai:dataCollection: The dataset was collected in three stages: curating passages from Wikipedia, crowdsourcing question-answer pairs using the Daemo platform with Amazon Mechanical Turk, and obtaining additional answers for evaluation purposes.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionRawData: Wikipedia articles (top 10,000 by PageRank, sampled 536 articles), from which paragraphs were extracted.
extraction.rai:dataManipulationProtocol: Paragraphs shorter than 500 characters were discarded. Images, figures, and tables were stripped. Articles were partitioned randomly into training (80%), development (10%), and test (10%) sets.
extraction.rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: Paragraphs were extracted from selected Wikipedia articles. Punctuation and articles (a, an, the) were ignored during evaluation metrics computation. For model training, when the correct answer was not a constituent in the constituency parse, the shortest constituent containing the correct answer was used as the target.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: Crowdworkers were tasked with asking and answering up to 5 questions per paragraph. Questions had to be entered in a text field, and answers had to be highlighted in the paragraph. Workers were encouraged to use their own words. For evaluation, at least 2 additional answers were obtained for each question in the development and test sets, where workers selected the shortest span answering the question.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationPlatform: Daemo platform (with Amazon Mechanical Turk as backend)
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationAnalysis: Human performance was assessed using inter-annotator agreement, achieving an F1 score of 86.8%. Mismatch occurred mostly due to inclusion/exclusion of non-essential phrases rather than fundamental disagreements.
extraction.rai:annotationsPerItem: At least 3 answers per question (1 primary + at least 2 additional for dev/test sets).
extraction.rai:annotatorDemographics: Crowdworkers were required to have a 97% HIT acceptance rate, a minimum of 1000 HITs, and be located in the United States or Canada.
extraction.rai:machineAnnotationTools: Stanford CoreNLP (used for constituency parses, POS tags, and NER tags for analysis and candidate answer generation)
extraction.rai:dataReleaseMaintenancePlan: The dataset is freely available at https://stanford-qa.com. The paper mentions SQuAD v1.0 and v1.1, indicating versioning.
extraction.rai:dataSocialImpact: The dataset presents a good challenge problem for future research in reading comprehension, with a significant gap between machine performance (51.0% F1) and human performance (86.8% F1), indicating room for advancement in modeling and learning.
extraction.rai:dataBiases: The dataset consists of questions posed by crowdworkers from the US and Canada, potentially reflecting biases in their language use and knowledge. The source articles are from English Wikipedia, which may have inherent biases in topic coverage and neutrality.
extraction.rai:dataLimitations: The dataset focuses on questions whose answers are entailed by the passage. It does not cover interpretative questions found in advanced standardized tests. The model performance degrades with increasing syntactic divergence and answer complexity, though human performance remains stable. The dataset is limited to English Wikipedia articles.
extraction.rai:dataUseCases: Training, Testing, Validation, Fine Tuning of machine reading comprehension and question answering models.
